record.title: The von Neumann neighborhood conjecture for graph codes
record.statement:
Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ vertices with vertex set $V$. Let $C$ be the binary linear code generated by $[I_n|A]$, and let $d(C)$ denote its minimum distance. For a nonempty subset $S$ of $V$, let $\operatorname{von}(S)$ denote its von Neumann neighborhood. **The von Neumann neighborhood conjecture.** If

$$
d(C)=|S|+|\operatorname{von}(S)|,
$$

then either $S=\operatorname{von}(S)$ or $S\cap\operatorname{von}(S)=\varnothing$. The observation preceding this conjecture verifies the claim for complete graphs, while its validity for general graphs is left open.
record.source_name: Sudipta Mallik and Bahattin Yildiz, “Isodual and Self-dual Codes from Graphs”, arXiv:1908.03513 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03513

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

record.title: The exact quasi-hyperbolicity constant conjecture for snowflaked Euclidean space
record.statement:
Let $0<\alpha<1$ and let $n\geq 2$. Equip $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the metric $d_2^\alpha$, where $d_2$ is the metric induced by the standard Euclidean norm, and let $C(\mathbb{R}^n,d_2^\alpha)$ denote its quasi-hyperbolicity constant. **Exact-value conjecture.**

$$
C(\mathbb{R}^n,d_2^\alpha)=2^{\alpha/2}.
$$

Numerical calculations suggest this exact value, improving the bounds $2^{\alpha/2}\leq C(\mathbb{R}^n,d_2^\alpha)\leq 2^{\min\{\alpha,1/2\}}$ established immediately beforehand. The claim remains unproved in the source.
record.source_name: George Dragomir and Andrew Nicas, “The Quasi-hyperbolicity Constant of a Metric Space”, arXiv:1908.04440 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04440

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

record.title: The $K_{4,6}$ extremal-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{4,6})$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $K_{4,6}$. **$K_{4,6}$ extremal-number conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{4,6})=o(n^{7/4}).
$$

The conjecture reflects the authors' belief that the geometric restrictions in the projective norm graph represent the limit of what algebraic constructions can offer, despite the occurrence of $K_{4,6}$ in $\operatorname{NG}(q,4)$; proving the asserted little-oh improvement remains open.
record.source_name: Tamás Mészáros, Lajos Rónyai and Tibor Szabó, “Singer difference sets and the projective norm graph”, arXiv:1908.05591 (2019).

record.title: The multiset-dimension upper-bound conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. The multiset dimension $md(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of an m-resolving set when one exists, and $md(G)=\infty$ otherwise.

**Multiset-dimension upper-bound conjecture.** If $G$ has finite multiset dimension, then

$$
md(G)\leq n-1.
$$

This conjecture was proposed in the cited earlier work as a sharpening of the immediate bound $md(G)\leq n$. The paper proves the stronger bound $md(T)\leq n-2$ for trees of diameter at least $2$ with finite multiset dimension, partially settling the conjecture in the tree case; the general graph statement remains open.
record.source_name: Yusuf Hafidh, Rizki Kurniawan, Suhadi Saputro, Rinovia Simanjuntak, Steven Tanujaya and Saladin Uttunggadewa, “Multiset Dimensions of Trees”, arXiv:1908.05879 (2019).

record.title: Minimum coprime number conjecture for GP(3k,k)
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, and let $GP(3k,k)$ be the generalized Petersen graph. Let $\mathfrak{pr}(G)$ denote its minimum coprime number. **The $GP(3k,k)$ minimum-coprime-number conjecture.** 
$$
\mathfrak{pr}(GP(3k,k))=\begin{cases}7k & \text{if } k \text{ is odd},\\ 7k+1 & \text{if } k \text{ is even}.\end{cases}
$$
 The source presents this as a conjecture motivated by independence-number bounds and reports verification only for small cases.
record.source_name: John Asplund and N. Bradley Fox, “Minimum Coprime Labelings of Generalized Petersen and Prism Graphs”, arXiv:1908.06051 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06051

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2019). “Additional cases of $GP(n,1)$ were proven to be prime in . Dean proved the conjecture that all ladders are prime.”

record.title: Minimum coprime number conjecture for stacked odd-gon prism graphs
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq 1$. The stacked $(2k+1)$-gon prism graph $Y_{2k+1,n}$ consists of $n$ stacked copies of a $(2k+1)$-cycle prism. Let $\mathfrak{pr}(G)$ denote the minimum coprime number. **The stacked-prism minimum-coprime-number conjecture.** 
$$
\mathfrak{pr}(Y_{2k+1,n})=2(k+1)n-1.
$$
 The proposed value follows the independence-number lower bound discussed in the source; the general construction is left conjectural.

record.title: Polynomial-time safe-set algorithm for clique-acyclic digraphs
record.statement:
A **clique acyclic digraph** is a digraph containing no directed triangle. Its **independence number** is the maximum size of a set of pairwise nonadjacent vertices. For a fixed constant independence number $\alpha$, there exists a polynomial-time algorithm to find a minimum safe set in such a digraph.

**Safe-set algorithm conjecture.** There exists a polynomial-time algorithm to find a minimum safe set in a clique acyclic digraph with a constant independence number $\alpha$.

The conjecture is motivated by a bound of Gyárfás et al. on the domination number of clique-acyclic digraphs with bounded independence number, together with the argument used earlier in the paper. Whether minimum safe sets can be found in polynomial time under these restrictions remains open.
record.source_name: Yandong Bai, Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Shinya Fujita and Anders Yeo, “Safe sets in digraphs”, arXiv:1908.06664 (2019).

record.title: Barát's good-coloring conjecture for subcubic graphs
record.statement: A **good coloring** of a graph is a 2-coloring of its vertices in blue and red such that the subgraph induced by the blue vertices has maximum degree at most $1$, the subgraph induced by the red vertices has minimum degree at least $1$, and the red subgraph contains no path on $4$ vertices. **Barát's conjecture.** Every subcubic graph on at least $7$ vertices has a good coloring. This is presented as a strengthening of Thomassen's conjecture and was motivated by Barát's results for generalized Petersen graphs and subcubic trees. The supplied text does not state whether this strengthening has been resolved; the paper's counterexamples to Thomassen's conjecture do not by themselves establish its status.
record.source_name: Thomas Bellitto, Tereza Klimošová, Martin Merker, Marcin Witkowski and Yelena Yuditsky, “Counterexamples to Thomassen's conjecture on decomposition of cubic graphs”, arXiv:1908.06697 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06697

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2019). “Wegner conjectured in 1977 that the square of every planar, cubic graph is 7-colorable and this was recently proved by Thomassen and independently by Hartke, Jahanbekam and Thomas .”

record.title: The degree bound conjecture for Snort on boards
record.statement: Let $B$ be a board for **Snort**, and let the degree of $B$ denote its maximum vertex degree. The temperature of a Snort position on $B$ measures the incentive to move. **The degree bound conjecture for Snort on boards.** The temperature of Snort on a board $B$ is at most the degree of $B$. This is proposed after computed temperatures for Snort on empty $2\times n$ grids; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Svenja Huntemann, Richard J. Nowakowski and Carlos Pereira dos Santos, “Bounding Game Temperature Using Confusion Intervals”, arXiv:1908.08471 (2019).

record.title: Chen--Lih--Wu's equitable Brooks conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected finite graph of maximum degree $\Delta \geqslant 1$. An **equitable $\Delta$-coloring** is a proper coloring with $\Delta$ color classes whose sizes differ by at most $1$.

**Chen--Lih--Wu's conjecture.** The graph $G$ has an equitable $\Delta$-coloring unless one of the following holds: $\Delta=2$ and $G$ is an odd cycle; $G \cong K_{\Delta+1}$; or $\Delta$ is odd and $G \cong K_{\Delta,\Delta}$.

This is an equitable analogue of Brooks's theorem. The conjecture remains open, and the paper studies measurable and Borel versions of related coloring results.
record.source_name: Anton Bernshteyn and Clinton T. Conley, “Equitable Colorings of Borel Graphs”, arXiv:1908.10475 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10475

record.title: The aperiodic Borel equitable Brooks conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an **aperiodic Borel graph**, meaning a Borel graph whose connected components are all infinite, with finite maximum degree $\Delta \geqslant 3$. Let $\mu$ be a $G$-invariant probability measure on $V(G)$. A **$\mu$-equitable $\Delta$-coloring** is a measurable proper $\Delta$-coloring whose color classes each have $\mu$-measure $1/\Delta$.

**Aperiodic Borel equitable Brooks conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a $\mu$-equitable $\Delta$-coloring.

The paper proves this under the additional hypothesis $d_\mu(G) \leqslant \Delta/5$, where $d_\mu(G)$ is the average degree, but the unrestricted statement remains open.
record.source_name: Anton Bernshteyn and Clinton T. Conley, “Equitable Colorings of Borel Graphs”, arXiv:1908.10475 (2021).

record.title: The global annulus conjecture for the first normalized Steklov eigenvalue
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda_{\epsilon}$ be a bounded connected planar annulus with two boundary components, and let $\lambda_{1}(\Lambda_{\epsilon})$ be its first nontrivial Steklov eigenvalue, given by the Steklov eigenvalue formula for annuli. **Global annulus conjecture.** Among bounded connected planar domains with two boundary components, the best planar annulus should be the one that realizes the maximum of

$$
\lambda_{1}(\Lambda_{\epsilon})|\partial\Lambda_{\epsilon}|.
$$

The paper identifies the annulus with inner radius $\epsilon_{0}$ from its preceding critical-domain proposition as a candidate for a global maximizer up to scaling, based on numerical evidence; the global claim remains unproved in the source.
record.source_name: Leoncio Rodriguez Quinones, “A Critical Domain For the First Normalized Nontrivial Steklov Eigenvalue Among Planar Annular Domains”, arXiv:1909.02121 (2022).

record.title: Gyárfás and Sárközy's minimum-degree conjecture for monochromatic components
record.statement:
Fix $k\geq 3$. Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree satisfying

$$
\delta(G)\geq\left(1-\frac{k-1}{k^2}\right)n.
$$

If the edges of $G$ are **$k$-coloured**, meaning that each edge receives one of $k$ colours, then **Gyárfás and Sárközy's conjecture.** there exists a monochromatic component of order at least

$$
\frac{n}{k-1}.
$$

This conjecture asks how far the complete-graph result for $k$-edge-colourings extends to graphs with large but not necessarily complete minimum degree. The source notes that Gyárfás and Sárközy had already proved the existence of some constant $\varepsilon_k>0$ for which minimum degree at least $(1-\varepsilon_k)n$ suffices; the stated threshold and conclusion remain the conjectured sharp form.
record.source_name: Hannah Guggiari and Alex Scott, “Monochromatic Components in Edge-Coloured Graphs with Large Minimum Degree”, arXiv:1909.09178 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.09178

record.title: Minimum minimizing index conjecture for doubled regular odd prime-gons
record.statement:
Let $X_p$ be the doubled regular $p$-gon, where $p$ is an odd prime. The **minimizing index** $\operatorname{minind}(X_p)$ is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $X_p$ admits a $1/k$-geodesic. **Minimum minimizing index conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{minind}(X_p)=2p.
$$

The paper establishes that doubled regular odd $n$-gons admit a $1/2n$-geodesic and therefore gives the upper bound $\operatorname{minind}(X_n)\leq 2n$; it also rules out half-geodesics. The conjecture asserts that this upper bound is sharp when $n=p$ is an odd prime.
record.source_name: Ian Adelstein and Adam Fong, “Closed geodesics on doubled polygons”, arXiv:1909.09275 (2019).

record.title: Surface bound conjecture for signed graph genus
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a surface, let $n_S$ be the largest order of a complete graph that embeds into $S$, and let $\gamma(G,\sigma)$ and $\gamma^*(G,\sigma)$ denote the relevant orientable and non-orientable genera of a signed graph. **Surface bound conjecture.** If $S$ is not the projective plane, then

$$
\gamma(G,\sigma) \leq \gamma(\pm K_S) \quad\text{and}\quad \gamma^*(G,\sigma) \leq \gamma^*(\pm K_S),
$$

and there are graphs for which equality holds. The statement is presented as a conjecture, with a theorem identified as a first result toward its proof; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Eckhard Steffen and Alexander Vogel, “Concepts of signed graph coloring”, arXiv:1909.09381 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1012.4117](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.4117).

record.title: The maximum-average-degree partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $c_1,c_2$ be positive real numbers, and let $\mathrm{mad}(G)$ denote the maximum average degree of $G$. A partition $V(G)=A\uplus B$ divides the vertex set into disjoint parts, with $G[A]$ and $G[B]$ the induced subgraphs on those parts.

**Maximum-average-degree partition conjecture.** If

$$
\mathrm{mad}(G)<c_1+c_2,
$$

then there exists a partition $V(G)=A\uplus B$ such that

$$
\mathrm{mad}(G[A])<c_1\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{mad}(G[B])<c_2.
$$

This is recalled in the source as a main open problem concerning partitions that decrease maximum average degree. The preceding corollaries provide special cases and applications, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Wojciech Nadara and Marcin Smulewicz, “Decreasing the maximum average degree by deleting an independent set or a d-degenerate subgraph”, arXiv:1909.10701 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10701

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2019). “As a main open problem in this area we recall the following one:”

record.title: Hadwiger–Boltyanski illumination conjecture for convex bodies
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{K}$ be a $d$-dimensional convex body in $\mathbb E^d$, where $d\geq 3$, and let $I(\mathbf{K})$ denote the smallest number of directions in $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ that illuminate every boundary point of $\mathbf{K}$. **Illumination conjecture.** The illumination number satisfies

$$
I(\mathbf{K})\leq 2^d,
$$

and equality holds only if $\mathbf{K}$ is an affine $d$-cube. This is a longstanding open problem in discrete geometry, known to be solved only in the plane; the conjecture is also related to the equivalent covering and separation conjectures.
record.source_name: Károly Bezdek and Zsolt Lángi, “From spherical to Euclidean illumination”, arXiv:1909.11884 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1602.06040](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.06040).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11884

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

record.title: The largest Carnot subgroup conjecture for Markov convexity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graded nilpotent Lie group, and let $H$ be its largest Carnot subgroup. For $p>0$, write $G$ as Markov $p$-convex when its metric space satisfies the Markov $p$-convexity inequality.

**Largest Carnot subgroup conjecture.** The set of $p$ for which $G$ is Markov $p$-convex is the same as the set of $p$ for which $H$ is Markov $p$-convex.

This conjecture proposes that Markov convexity of a graded nilpotent Lie group is completely determined by its largest Carnot subgroup. The source presents it as an additional conjecture, with no resolution stated.
record.source_name: Chris Gartland, “Estimates on the Markov Convexity of Carnot Groups and Quantitative Nonembeddability”, arXiv:1909.12399 (2019).

record.title: The maximum-degree-two rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f_G(n,m)$ denote the least number of independent $n$-sets in a graph $G$ that guarantees a rainbow independent set of size $m$. **Maximum-degree-two conjecture.** If $G$ has maximum degree $2$, then

$$
f_G(n,n-1)=n-1.
$$

Equivalently, every $n-1$ matchings of size $n$ in a graph of maximum degree $2$ have a full rainbow matching. The source identifies this as a special case of the exceptional-line-graph conjecture and notes that the one-cycle case follows from the chordal-graph theorem.

record.title: The refined bounded-degree conjecture for full rainbow sets
record.statement:
Let $f_{\mathcal D(k)}(n)$ denote the full-rainbow parameter for the class $\mathcal D(k)$ of graphs with maximum degree at most $k$, and let $q$ be the quantity used in the source's preceding discussion. **Refined bounded-degree conjecture.** For $k>2$ and $n>3$,

$$
f_{\mathcal D(k)}(n)=q(n-1)+1.
$$

The statement appears in the paper's summary of open problems, but the supplied context does not define $q$ or explicitly identify $f_{\mathcal D(k)}(n)$ with the two-parameter notation.

record.title: Cyclotomic maximum-or-minimum coefficient conjecture
record.statement: For a cyclotomic polynomial, call a coefficient **non-zero** when it is not equal to zero. **Cyclotomic maximum-or-minimum coefficient conjecture.** Every non-zero integer occurs either as the maximum coefficient or as the minimum coefficient of some cyclotomic polynomial. The paper presents this as a conjectural extension from prescribed heights to prescribed extreme coefficients; its status is open.

record.title: Independent domination conjecture for Cartesian products
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be undirected graphs. Write $\gamma(G)$ for the domination number of a graph, and let $i(G)$ denote its **independent domination number**, the smallest size of an independent dominating set of $G$. The Cartesian product $G\square H$ has vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$. The **independent domination conjecture.**

$$
i(G\square H)\geq \min\{i(G)\gamma(H),\gamma(G)i(H)\}.
$$

This is an analogue of Vizing's conjecture for independent domination and would imply Vizing's conjecture. The stronger product inequality $i(G\square H)\geq i(G)i(H)$ is known to fail for some graphs, so this formulation avoids that obstruction; its resolution is not supplied in the source.

record.title: Connectivity–minimum-degree conjecture for Fibonacci $(p,r)$-cubes
record.statement: Let $I\Gamma_{n}^{(p,r)}$ and $O\Gamma_{n}^{(p,r)}$ be the Fibonacci-like cubes considered above, with $p\geq1$, $r\geq1$, and $n\geq1$. **Connectivity–minimum-degree conjecture.** The connectivity of $I\Gamma_{n}^{(p,r)}$ and $O\Gamma_{n}^{(p,r)}$ equals their respective minimum degree. This conjecture proposes that both graph families attain the standard upper bound relating vertex connectivity to minimum degree; the paper gives no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: The super-approximation conjecture for finitely generated linear groups
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)$ be a finitely generated group. For each modulus $q$, let $X_q$ be the corresponding Cayley graph of the reduction of $\Gamma$ modulo $q$, and let $T_S^{(q)}$ denote the associated averaging operator. The group $\Gamma$ has **super-approximation** if there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that

$$
\|T_S^{(q)}\|\leq 1-\epsilon,\quad \forall q\in\mathbb N.
$$

Let $\mathbb G$ be the Zariski closure of $\Gamma$; its identity component is **perfect** when

$$
[\mathbb G^\circ,\mathbb G^\circ]=\mathbb G^\circ.
$$

**Super-approximation conjecture.** The group $\Gamma$ has super-approximation, without restriction on the moduli, if and only if the Zariski closure $\mathbb G$ of $\Gamma$ has perfect identity component.
This conjecture extends the known results for square-free moduli and prime powers, and would characterize super-approximation for all moduli in terms of the algebraic structure of the Zariski closure.
record.source_name: Lam Pham and Xin Zhang, “Logarithmic bounds for the diameters of some Cayley graphs”, arXiv:1910.05718 (2021).

record.title: The nonchalant-word infinitude conjecture for three-letter alphabets
record.statement: Let $\mathbb A$ be a fixed ordered alphabet, and recursively construct the sequence of nonchalant words by starting with $G_1=\mathtt a$ and, at each step, inserting the earliest possible letter in the rightmost possible position so that the resulting word remains square-free. **Nonchalant-word infinitude conjecture.** The sequence of nonchalant words over a $3$-letter alphabet is infinite. This conjecture concerns whether the greedy square-free extension procedure ever stops; the paper gives initial examples and motivates the question through a recursive construction based on computer verification.

record.title: The EKR conjecture for unions of length-2 paths
record.statement: Let $r \leq n$, and let $G$ be the vertex-disjoint union of $n$ paths each of length $2$. A family of independent $r$-sets of $G$ is intersecting if any two of its members have a common vertex, and $G$ is $r$-EKR when every such family has size at most the largest star. **The EKR conjecture for unions of length-2 paths.** If $r \leq n$, then $G$ is $r$-EKR. The paper has proved this property under a stronger restriction on $r$ and conjectures that the bound $r \leq n$ is sufficient.

record.title: Cramér's weak conjecture on maximal prime gaps
record.statement:
Let $p_n$) denote the $n^{th}$ prime, and for $X$ consider the largest consecutive prime gap with $p_n\le X$:

$$
\sup_{p_n\le X}(p_{n+1}-p_n).
$$

**Cramér's weak conjecture.** The largest such gap satisfies

$$
\sup_{p_n\le X}(p_{n+1}-p_n)=(\log X)^{2+o(1)}.
$$

The source presents this as a weaker form of Cramér's original conjecture, which is no longer fully believed; the stated weak form remains open.
record.source_name: James Maynard, “Gaps between primes”, arXiv:1910.13450 (2019).

record.title: The conjecture on the minimum eigenvalue derivative for block-Toeplitz symbols
record.statement:
Let $\deg>0$, $j>0$, and $z>0$. Let $\hat{f}_{z,j}$ be the symbol appearing in the paper, and let $\lambda”_{\rm min}(\hat{f}_{z,j})|_{0}$ denote the second derivative at $0$ of its minimum eigenvalue. **The minimum-eigenvalue derivative conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_{z,\deg}>0$ such that

$$
\left.\lambda”_{\rm min}(\hat{f}_{z,j})\right|_{0}=c_{z,\deg}\left(\frac{z^2}{2}\right)^j.
$$

This conjecture is used to extend the condition-number analysis from polynomial degree $2$ to higher degrees; it was numerically verified in the paper for $\deg=3,4$, but no general proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Marco Donatelli, Paola Ferrari, Isabella Furci, Stefano Serra Capizzano and Debora Sesana, “Multigrid methods for block-Toeplitz linear systems: convergence analysis and applications”, arXiv:1910.13792 (2019).

record.title: The Standard (2,2)-Conjecture on decomposition into two {1,2}-weight colourable subgraphs
record.statement: Let a graph be **$\{1,2\}$-weight colourable** if its edges can be assigned weights from $\{1,2\}$ so that adjacent vertices receive distinct sums of the weights on their incident edges. A graph has an isolated edge if one of its edges forms a connected component on two vertices, and an isolated triangle if a connected component is a triangle. **Standard $(2,2)$-Conjecture.** Every graph without isolated edges and isolated triangles can be decomposed into two $\{1,2\}$-weight colourable subgraphs. The paper proves this conjecture for graphs with sufficiently large minimum degree, while the unrestricted statement is not resolved by the supplied context.
record.source_name: Jakub Przybyło, “On the Standard (2,2)-Conjecture”, arXiv:1911.00867 (2019).

record.title: Persistence threshold conjecture for species and environments
record.statement:
Consider the Moran model with a finite set of species and a finite set of environments. Persistence means that the system persists rather than becoming extinct.

**Persistence threshold conjecture.** Persistence of the system is possible if and only if the number of environments is at least the number of species.

The paper states that this assertion has been proved for systems with two or three species, while configurations with three species and three environments can exhibit persistence. Explicit conditions for persistence in general remain unknown.
record.source_name: Arnaud Guillin, Arnaud Personne and Edouard Strickler, “Persistence in the Moran model with random switching”, arXiv:1911.01108 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01108

record.title: The matching bound conjecture for 1-planar graphs of minimum degree 6
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a fixed positive integer. A **1-planar graph** is a graph that admits a drawing in which each edge is crossed at most once. Consider a 1-planar graph with minimum degree at least $6$ and $n\geq N$ vertices. **Matching bound conjecture.** Every such graph has a matching of size at least

$$
\frac{3}{7}n+O(1).
$$

The preceding construction gives 1-planar graphs of minimum degree $6$ whose maximum matching has size at most $\frac{3}{7}n+\frac{4}{7}$, so the conjectured linear coefficient would be tight up to an additive constant. The source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Therese Biedl and John Wittnebel, “Matchings in 1-planar graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:1911.04603 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04603

record.title: The valuation conjecture for dp-finite fields
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an unstable dp-finite field embedded in a monster model $\mathbb{K} \succeq K$. Let $I_K$ be the group of $K$-infinitesimals, equivalently the smallest additive subgroup of $\mathbb{K}$ that is type-definable over $K$ and satisfies

$$
\operatorname{dp-rk}(I_K)=\operatorname{dp-rk}(\mathbb{K}).
$$

For an additive subgroup $J$ of $\mathbb{K}$, define

$$
\operatorname{Stab}(J):=\{a\in\mathbb{K}:a\cdot J\subseteq J\}.
$$

**Valuation conjecture.** The group $I_K$ is an ideal in a valuation ring on $\mathbb{K}$; equivalently, $\operatorname{Stab}(I_K)$ is a valuation ring.

This is the main gap in extending the classification strategy for unstable dp-minimal fields to dp-finite fields. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Will Johnson, “Dp-finite fields III: inflators and directories”, arXiv:1911.04727 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04727

record.title: Birkar's bounded-weight conjecture for weighted blowups
record.statement: Let $\mathbb A^d_{\mathbf n}$ be the weighted blowup of $\mathbb A^d$ at $0\in\mathbb A^d$ with coprime, meaning primitive, weights $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_d)\in\mathbb N^d$. A variety has $\varepsilon$-log canonical singularities when all its log discrepancies are at least $\varepsilon$. **Birkar's conjecture.** If $\mathbb A^d_{\mathbf n}$ has $\varepsilon$-log canonical singularities, then the smallest of the weights is bounded by a constant depending only on $d$ and $\varepsilon$. This conjecture predicts a uniform bound on the smallest weight in weighted blowups with controlled singularities; the paper proves such a bound, so the conjecture is resolved.
record.source_name: G. K. Sankaran and Francisco Santos, “Blowups with log canonical singularities”, arXiv:1911.06435 (2020).

record.title: Critical-regime clique-count conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
record.statement:
Let $n=a(r+1)+b$, and let $m$ satisfy

$$
\frac{nr}{2} \ge m>a \binom{r+1}{2} + \binom{b}{2}.
$$

For fixed $t$, or for $k=\sum_{t \ge 2} k_t$, consider graphs of order $n$, size $m$, and maximum degree at most $r$. **Critical-regime clique-count conjecture.** Any graph maximizing the chosen quantity can be represented as $(a-1)K_{r+1}+H$. This concerns the remaining, or critical, regime after the known cases in which the extremal graph is a union of copies of $K_{r+1}$ and a colex graph; the source provides no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: The stable-structure tail conjecture for median dynamics on the square lattice
record.statement:
Consider median dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, with $\eta_\infty(0)$ denoting the limiting opinion at the origin. **Stable-structure tail conjecture.** 

$$
\limsup_{\alpha\to0}\frac{\mathbb{P}[\eta_\infty(0)\in[0,\alpha]]}{\alpha^4}<\infty.
$$

The exponent $4$ comes from the smallest stable structures, namely $2\times2$ squares, and the conjecture asserts that these structures determine the order of the density near zero.
record.source_name: Gideon Amir, Rangel Baldasso and Nissan Beilin, “Majority dynamics and the median process: connections, convergence and some new conjectures”, arXiv:1911.08613 (2023).

record.title: Bolza surface conjecture for extremal-length systoles in genus 2
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}_2$ denote the moduli space of conformal classes of closed genus-$2$ surfaces. For a conformal class $X\in\mathcal{M}_2$, let $\operatorname{sys}_{\operatorname{EL}}(X)$ be the minimum extremal length of an essential simple closed curve on $X$. **Bolza surface conjecture.** The maximum of $\operatorname{sys}_{\operatorname{EL}}$ in genus $2$ is attained by the conformal class of the Bolza surface. The Bolza surface is known to realize the maximum of the hyperbolic systole in genus $2$ and also appears as a maximizer for other notions of systolic length; whether it maximizes the extremal-length systole remains open.
record.source_name: Dídac Martínez-Granado and Franco Vargas Pallete, “Comparing hyperbolic and extremal lengths for shortest curves”, arXiv:1911.09078 (2025).

record.title: The volume-product conjecture for finite metric spaces
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a metric space with $n+1$ points. Let $\mathcal F(M)$ be its Lipschitz-free space, let $B_{\mathcal F(M)}$ be the unit ball of this $n$-dimensional space, and define

$$
\mathcal P(M):=\mathcal P(B_{\mathcal F(M)}).
$$

**Volume-product conjecture for finite metric spaces.** One has

$$
\mathcal P(M)\geq \mathcal P(B_1^n).
$$

Here $B_1^n$ is the cross-polytope, whose volume product equals that of the cube and is the conjectured minimum among symmetric convex bodies. This is presented as the paper's main conjecture for the volume products of Lipschitz-free spaces; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Matthew Alexander, Matthieu Fradelizi, Luis C. García-Lirola and Artem Zvavitch, “Geometry and volume product of finite dimensional Lipschitz-free spaces”, arXiv:1911.10642 (2020).

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for eigenvalues of the Neumann–Poincaré operator on planar corners
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a piecewise $C^3$ Jordan curve with finitely many corners, whose angles lie strictly between $0$ and $\pi$. Let $K \colon H^{1/2}(\Gamma) \to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ be the Neumann–Poincaré operator. **Finiteness conjecture.** The operator $K$ has finitely many eigenvalues. This is an outstanding question for planar domains with corners; existing constructions exhibit eigenvalues embedded in the absolutely continuous essential spectrum, but do not suggest the existence of infinitely many eigenvalues.
record.source_name: Karl-Mikael Perfekt, “Plasmonic eigenvalue problem for corners: limiting absorption principle and absolute continuity in the essential spectrum”, arXiv:1911.12294 (2020).

record.title: Jones' Conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. A **cycle packing** is a set of vertex-disjoint cycles in $G$; let $\operatorname{cp}(G)$ denote its maximum size. A **feedback vertex set** is a set $S$ of vertices such that $G-S$ is a forest; let $\operatorname{fvs}(G)$ denote the minimum size of a feedback vertex set.

**Jones' Conjecture.** Every planar graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{fvs}(G)\leqslant 2\cdot\operatorname{cp}(G).
$$

This conjecture concerns the relationship between cycle packing and feedback vertex sets, strengthening the general Erdős–Pósa-type bound for planar graphs. The source confirms the conjecture for subcubic planar graphs, but the general planar case remains open.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, François Dross, Tomáš Masařík, Wojciech Nadara, Marcin Pilipczuk and Michał Pilipczuk, “Jones' Conjecture in subcubic graphs”, arXiv:1912.01570 (2019).

record.title: Gan–Loh–Sudakov triangle extremal conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $d$. Write

$$
n=q(d+1)+r,\qquad 0\le r\le d.
$$

Here $q$ and $r$ are the quotient and remainder in the division of $n$ by $d+1$. **Gan–Loh–Sudakov's conjecture.** The number of triangles in $G$ is at most

$$
q{d+1 \choose 3}+{r \choose 3}.
$$

The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is resolved by the paper itself, so the claimed bound is a theorem rather than an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Zachary Chase, “The Maximum Number of Triangles in a Graph of Given Maximum Degree”, arXiv:1912.01600 (2020).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1809.03729](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03729), [arXiv:1709.06163](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06163), [arXiv:1405.1322](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.1322).
